items.title: The smooth locus of a reduced locally algebraic scheme over a perfect field is a dense open and equals the regular locus
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a perfect field k and a locally algebraic reduced k-scheme X, the lemma identifies the set of points where X over Spec(k) is smooth with the set of points whose local ring is regular, and shows that this set is a dense open subscheme (statement lines 4729-4738). The proof separates the three claims: the equality of the two sets is a direct consequence of the algebra criterion relating smoothness at a point to separability of the residue field over a perfect field; openness is the openness of the smooth locus; and density is given twice, once through the generic points of X, whose local rings are fields and hence regular, and once by combining the geometric reducedness of X over a perfect field with the dense smooth open criterion proved just before (proof lines 4740-4753). The claim is H2: three separate claims, each settled by a standard input, with the double argument for density reflecting the two available routes, and no step referred to the reader beyond the cited immediate consequence.
